record.paper_title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Twice-differentiable planar convex function with no Hessian limit
record.original_question: Does there exist a convex function f: R^2 -> R that is twice differentiable in a neighborhood of the origin but whose Hessian Hf(x) has no limit as x -> 0? This is proposed as the natural finite-dimensional starting case for the broader open problem about loss of Hessian convergence for convex functions.

evidence.quote: It seems that an investigation might start with looking for an answer to the following question: does there exist a convex function f from R2 to R, derivable two times around the origin, for which the limit lim x→ 0 Hf (x) does not exist?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Does there exist a convex function $f : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ that is twice differentiable at every point of some open neighborhood $U$ of the origin (so that the Hessian matrix $H_f(x) = \big(\partial^2 f/\partial x_i \partial x_j(x)\big)_{1\le i,j\le 2}$ is well defined for every $x \in U$), and for which the limit
$$\lim_{x \to 0} H_f(x)$$
fails to exist (in the space of $2\times 2$ symmetric matrices)?

Equivalently: construct, or prove the nonexistence of, a convex $C^1$ function $f$ on a neighborhood of $0 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ whose second-order partial derivatives all exist pointwise on that neighborhood but do not all converge as $x \to 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of this specific question concerning the existence of a planar convex function twice differentiable in a neighborhood of the origin whose Hessian has no limit at 0. The question is presented as a natural finite-dimensional starting point for a broader open problem on Hessian convergence of convex functions, and no construction or impossibility proof was located.

status_evidence.title: Second-Order Convex Analysis (Rockafellar)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses second-order behavior of convex functions; standard reference but does not resolve pointwise Hessian convergence at a point of twice differentiability.
status_evidence.claim: Existing second-order convex analysis literature does not provide a direct answer to this specific question.
